headline: $63B Broadcom–Anthropic chip financing extends the AI rebound; Nasdaq +1.2%, Boeing caps Dow
summary: A narrow, tech-led advance on the eve of the Fed. Stocks opened mixed, then firmed through the morning as chipmakers rallied for a third day and upbeat consumer-confidence and durable-goods data landed, with the S&P 500 holding most of a 0.7% midday gain into the close. Tech led and energy lagged as oil slid below $100; advancers beat decliners about 1.8 to 1 on the NYSE, yet most S&P 500 members fell and Boeing's slide left the Dow flat.
drivers: Broadcom deal keeps the AI trade going

Banks including Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley plus Blackstone lined up $63 billion to finance Broadcom AI chips and networking gear leased to Anthropic, a day after its IPO filing. Broadcom rose about 4%, AMD 5.4%, Intel 3.6% and Micron 2.8%, while Nvidia lagged at +0.9%; the SOX gained about 3% for a third straight rise and neocloud CoreWeave jumped 7.9%.

Talks in Tehran between Iran, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey revived hopes of ending the US–Iran war, sending WTI down 1.8% to $99.90 and Brent 1.7% to $113.88. Energy was the weakest sector, refiners fell, and airlines and cruise lines rallied (Royal Caribbean +5.5% after raising its profit outlook).
Strong data, steady yields before the Fed

Consumer confidence jumped to 91.7 against forecasts near 81 and September durable-goods orders rose 1.8%, with computer orders up again. The 10-year Treasury yield ended little changed near 4.99% after a solid 5-year auction, with a Fed hold at 3.75–4% widely expected Wednesday and a December hike still priced.
Earnings split: Boeing sinks, UPS soars

Boeing fell 10.7%, its worst day since 2020, on a wider-than-expected loss and a delayed 737 production ramp, single-handedly holding the Dow flat; Xylem lost 14.2% on a cut forecast and Sherwin-Williams 2.7% on a profit miss. UPS climbed 5.8% after raising its outlook, and Meta slipped 1.6% after enlarging its equity raise to $97.5 billion, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom offering to buy up to $5 billion.
week: Two days into the week the S&P 500 is up 1.3% and the Nasdaq 2.0%, leaving the S&P 500 about 1.2% below its early-October record; the backdrop is a 10-year yield near 5%, oil around $100 and a Fed that hiked in September, with markets pricing another hike in December.
watch: Next: the Fed decides Wednesday Oct 28 (a hold is widely expected; Chair Warsh's press conference is the focus), with Alphabet, Microsoft and SK hynix reporting the same day, then Amazon, Intel and Samsung on Thursday alongside the ECB, GDP and inflation data, and the Nov 3 midterms.
